title: Four finite-level arrows
statement:
Use the four objects $A_n,B_n,C_n,D_n$ and the notation $K_n,E=L(g')^*K,E_n=L(g'_n)^*K_n$ of [def-weil-pbc-four-corners]. Thus $f:X\to Y$ is proper, $f':X'\to Y'$ is its base change, $g:Y'\to Y$, $g':X'\to X$, $P_n=A/I^n$ is finite and perfect over $A$, and all operations use the specified compatible coefficient identifications for $A_T=\varprojlim_m(P_m)_T$ and $(P_n)_T$. Tensors are uncompleted derived extensions of scalars. Retain the specified finite-coefficient etale-origin data [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness]
$$L_n\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},P_n),\qquad \alpha_n:\nu_X^*L_n\xrightarrow{\sim}K_n\quad(n\geq1).$$
In particular $K_n$ is bounded below. No uniform lower bound or compatibility between the witnesses for different $n$ is required to define these individual arrows.

For an edge $u:U\to V$ put $S_{T,n}(F)=F\otimes^L_{A_T}(P_n)_T$. Write
$$\chi_{u,F,n}:Lu_n^*S_{V,n}(F)\xrightarrow{\sim}S_{U,n}(Lu^*F)$$
for the canonical coefficient-reduction/pullback comparison. It is the pullback/tensor comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] with the coefficient identifications of [def-weil-pbc-four-corners], in the displayed direction. Concretely on a K-flat representative $Q$ with flat terms [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], it is the ordinary tensor identification
$$u_n^*(Q\otimes_{A_V}(P_n)_V)\longrightarrow (u^*Q)\otimes_{A_U}(P_n)_U.$$
Both sides compute the stated derived objects: apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] also to the identity-topos ring map $A_T\to(P_n)_T$ to see that scalar extension preserves K-flat complexes with flat terms; [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] identifies the ordinary tensor of such a resolution with derived scalar extension. The same pullback lemma applies to $u$ and $u_n$. The tensor balancing map is $(P_n)_U$-linear by the compatibility $\pi_{U,n}c_u=c_{u,n}u^{-1}\pi_{V,n}$ of the coefficient identifications, so this is a comparison in $D(U_{\mathrm{proet}},P_n)$, not just after forgetting coefficients. Let $\delta_n:S_{X',n}(E)\xrightarrow{\sim}E_n$ be the comparison of [def-weil-pbc-four-corners]; in this notation it is $\chi_{g',K,n}^{-1}$.

For $H\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ define the finite-coefficient projection map
$$p_{f,H,n}:S_{Y,n}(Rf_*H)\longrightarrow Rf_{*,n}S_{X,n}(H)$$
as the adjunct under $Lf_n^*\dashv Rf_{*,n}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] of the explicit composite
$$Lf_n^*S_{Y,n}(Rf_*H)\xrightarrow{\chi_{f,Rf_*H,n}}S_{X,n}(Lf^*Rf_*H)\xrightarrow{S_{X,n}(\varepsilon_{f,H})}S_{X,n}(H).$$
Here $\varepsilon_{f,H}$ is the ambient counit. Use the same definition for $f'$ and $H\in D(X'_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$. Under restriction of scalars along $A_T\to(P_n)_T$, the adjunction comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction] identifies this adjunct with $\pi_{f,H,(P_n)_Y}$ of [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-map]. The perfect-coefficient theorem [lemma-weil-pbc-perfect-projection-formula] supplies its inverse, and restriction of scalars reflects isomorphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction]. Thus each $p_{f,H,n}$, and likewise $p_{f',H,n}$, is an isomorphism.

Define the four finite-level arrows, all in $D(Y'_{\mathrm{proet}},P_n)$, by
$$\begin{aligned}
h_n&=Lg_n^*(p_{f,K,n}):A_n\xrightarrow{\sim}B_n,\\
h'_n&=Rf'_{*,n}(\delta_n)\circ p_{f',E,n}:C_n\xrightarrow{\sim}D_n,\\
v_n&=S_{Y',n}(\operatorname{Ex}^{A}_{\square,K})\circ\chi_{g,Rf_*K,n}:A_n\longrightarrow C_n,\\
v'_n&=\operatorname{Ex}^{P_n}_{\square,K_n}:B_n\xrightarrow{\sim}D_n.
\end{aligned}$$
The transformation $\operatorname{Ex}^{A}$ is the ambient ringed exchange of [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange]. The same definition applied to the finite coefficient sheaves $(P_n)_T$ gives $\operatorname{Ex}^{P_n}$: its adjunct is
$$Lf_n'^*Lg_n^*Rf_{*,n}K_n\xrightarrow{\theta_{\square,n}}Lg_n'^*Lf_n^*Rf_{*,n}K_n\xrightarrow{Lg_n'^*\varepsilon_{f,n,K_n}}Lg_n'^*K_n.$$
The coefficient identifications make $Lg_n^*$ and $Lg_n'^*$ the exact inverse images, so the hypotheses of [thm-weil-pbc-finite-level-proetale] apply with finite ring $P_n$, proper $f$, and witness $(L_n,\alpha_n)$. That theorem certifies that this canonical $v'_n$ is invertible; it is the exchange transported using the specified witness and is unchanged by replacing that witness by an isomorphic one. The definition makes no assertion that $v_n$ is invertible or that the four-arrow square commutes.

note:
*Source:* the four arrows are Stacks entries. The exchange morphisms are the
canonical base change map $Lg^*Rf_*K\to Rf'_*L(g')^*K$ of Cohomology on
Sites, Remark 21.19.3 ([Tag
07A7](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07A7)), constructed there in full
generality for a commutative diagram of ringed topoi as the adjoint of
$L(g')^*$ of the adjunction map $Lf^*Rf_*K\to K$; $v_n$ is its tensor
reduction along $P_n$, and $v'_n$ is its finite-level form, an isomorphism
by Theorem 61.30.1 ([Tag 09C9](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C9))
applied to $K_n$ with its etale-origin witness. The projection-formula
companions $h_n,h'_n$ are the map of Equation 21.50.0.1 ([Tag
0B56](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B56)) and its
perfect-coefficient form, Lemma 21.50.1 ([Tag
0944](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0944)). Difference of generality:
Stacks' base change map is stated for ringed topoi with no completeness
hypothesis and no coefficient tower, and is not asserted to be an
isomorphism — the isomorphism is Stacks' proper base change theorem 61.30.1,
which states no construction of the map; the required identification of
$v'_n$ with the finite-level form of the specified etale-origin witness, and
the assembly of the two exchange arrows with their two projection-formula
companions on the corners of one square, are the blueprint's presentation at
the finite coefficient rings $P_n=A/I^n$.

split_report.summary: Expanded the four maps as explicit finite-coefficient adjoints and composites, retaining quotient actions. Made the implicit bounded-below etale-origin witness explicit. Reused the existing perfect projection and finite-level PBC theorems. Added one general ring-sheaf change-of-coefficients adjunction comparison, since existing scalar-comparison nodes only cover constant coefficient rings. No proof steps for a definition.
split_report.blueprint: The four displayed arrows: h_n is pullback of the finite projection adjunct; h′_n includes the E reduction identification; v_n is the specified tensor reduction with its source comparison; v′_n is the canonical finite exchange with its stated witness. The source note is realized by cited existing projection and finite PBC theorems.
